The wait matched exactly request 3, although commits are not ordered across request numbers and a later request can commit first; pull request 907 removes that assumption, accepting request 3 or any later one. That does not cure the cell, which stays intermittently red. On some runners the origin's durable store runs 10 to 20 times slower while the cell runs, and the gap requests, repair hints and repair sends miss the origin's waits; nothing is lost, and renewals stop at request 4. Measured with pull request 909's batch diagnostics on three runs, 45723714914 (3.94 ms/op, passed), 45723711046 (32.07 ms/op, passed) and 45723719146 (41.82 ms/op, failed): the median control claim in the two cells cost 14, 24 and 239 ms, the median repair-hint claim 190, 34 and 2,383 ms, and the longest durable batch ran 3.3, 11.4 and 21.4 s; the failed run had single ACK replays of 3.8 s, selection phases of 3.5 s and release phases of 2.8 s. The family's per-operation median does not show this. A control that loses the held message's version fence is expedited into the batch already running without counting toward its page, which does lengthen a batch, but that was the main cause in one of the failed run's seven batches of 5 s or longer, and bounding the batch would not have brought that run's four late commands inside their waits: one was a direct admission outside any batch that finished 251 ms late, two parked before the bound would apply or without its trigger, and one is borderline on an estimate. Not established: why the store slows in these cells, and what the direct admission path costs, which has no timing. Three runs are a small sample, and a batch aborted at teardown hides its unfinished claims. Earlier evidence: observation run 45690968763 on main 99016dc5a (41.88 ms/op) failed relayed-unreceipted-gap-renewal; with a 50 s lifetime and a 25 s hold, since withdrawn, runs 45707321821 (29.04 ms/op) and 45707356002 (39.24 ms/op) failed both cells and run 45707352091 (38.6 ms/op) passed.

Two causes. Fixed in pull request 882: the receiver had to count its arrivals inside a fixed window that opened before the sender's send loop, and the loop, which awaits each send and then pauses, ran several times slower on a GitHub runner than the window assumed; the receiver now counts after the sender's cue and the loop's budget is derived from its send count. Open: in run 45111742994 the sender's reconnect never reached RTC readiness. The receiver saw the sender return before it had accepted the layout that recorded her departure, dialled on the stale layout and replaced its connection twice, and the sender answered a retired connection's offer last, so the pair never established. That is an RTC runtime defect, not the scenario's.
